reason: The cited evidence shows that dynamic loading in Al0.3CoCrFeNi leads to high work hardening and resistance to shear localization, and mentions mechanical twinning as a contributing mechanism (E2). However, E1 on NbTaHfTiZrV0.5 only reports dislocation slip-controlled deformation without twinning, and neither passage provides direct evidence that rapid loading enhances dislocation slip that triggers twinning, nor that twins act as barriers to increase strain hardening under dynamic conditions. The key causal premises are thus only partially supported.
premises: Rapid loading enhances dislocation slip that triggers mechanical twinning in HEAs
Twins act as barriers to dislocation motion, increasing strain hardening
Enhanced strain hardening suppresses shear localization
The mechanism applies to single-phase HEAs with low stacking fault energy
Dynamic loading increases twin formation compared to quasi-static loading
